summary: 2+2 channel DJ mixer with 3-band total-kill EQ, VCF filters, balanced XLR main outputs, booth/record outputs and a built-in 24-bit/96 kHz four-stereo-channel USB soundcard (plus X:LINK), usable as the audio interface for Traktor Scratch Pro DVS.
identityNotes: Confirmed by the owner: the unit is the Xone:23C (with the built-in USB soundcard), not the analog-only Xone:23. The profile id stays 'allen-heath-xone-23' so existing databases keep their unit and results. Analog layout and features are shared with the Xone:23. No MIDI DIN ports. The 23C has a USB B socket and an X:LINK port on the rear panel.

A&H's 'XONE:23C USB ASIO driver' is needed to reach all soundcard channels on Windows; the driver also offers a 'Core Audio' mode described as fully class compliant (documented for macOS; behaviour of the plain Windows class-compliant path is unverified). software.name: Traktor Pro
software.notes: The 23C is listed as Traktor certified by retailers (e.g. https://mannys.com.au/allen-and-heath-xone-23c-traktor-certified-dj-mixer-w-usb-i-o) although another source says it is not NI approved hardware; either way Traktor Scratch Pro uses the 23C soundcard through its ASIO driver (Preferences > Audio Setup). Timecode vinyl is MK2 (owner confirmed).

tests.title: Channel 1 signal health: line and phono
tests.why: Isolates a dead or noisy channel input stage.
steps: Feed a stereo source into channel 1 LINE, set the input switch to LINE, trim at 12 o'clock.
Take main output (record out or master) into the PC input; run signal health.
Repeat with PHONO and a turntable.

tests.title: Channel 1 gain structure and meter
tests.why: Verifies trim and fader give usable range with no clipping before the master.
steps: Play music at 0 dB; turn channel 1 trim up until the channel LED meter just peaks green/amber.
Sweep trim fully down: signal gone; fully up: no distortion at peaks if channel fader is down.
Compare to the other channel with the same source.

tests.title: Channel 1 EQ and kill
tests.why: The Xone:23 EQs are total-kill; a kill that leaves signal means a faulty pot or switch.
steps: Play full-range music.
Turn HI fully down: highs vanish; MID fully down: mid vanishes; LO fully down: bass vanishes.
Turn each fully up: boost without distortion; centre detent is flat.
Rotate each pot slowly: no crackle or dropouts.

tests.title: Channel 1 line fader
tests.why: Worn faders crackle or lose a channel.
steps: Play music, move the fader slowly end to end: no crackle, no channel loss, smooth travel.
Check silence at fully down.

tests.title: Channel 2 signal health: line and phono
tests.why: Isolates a dead or noisy channel input stage.
steps: Feed a stereo source into channel 2 LINE, set the input switch to LINE, trim at 12 o'clock.
Take main output (record out or master) into the PC input; run signal health.
Repeat with PHONO and a turntable.

tests.title: Channel 2 gain structure and meter
tests.why: Verifies trim and fader give usable range with no clipping before the master.
steps: Play music at 0 dB; turn channel 2 trim up until the channel LED meter just peaks green/amber.
Sweep trim fully down: signal gone; fully up: no distortion at peaks if channel fader is down.
Compare to the other channel with the same source.

tests.title: Channel 2 EQ and kill
tests.why: The Xone:23 EQs are total-kill; a kill that leaves signal means a faulty pot or switch.
steps: Play full-range music.
Turn HI fully down: highs vanish; MID fully down: mid vanishes; LO fully down: bass vanishes.
Turn each fully up: boost without distortion; centre detent is flat.
Rotate each pot slowly: no crackle or dropouts.

tests.title: Channel 2 line fader
tests.why: Worn faders crackle or lose a channel.
steps: Play music, move the fader slowly end to end: no crackle, no channel loss, smooth travel.
Check silence at fully down.

tests.title: Main output L/R balance
tests.why: A level mismatch between left and right output indicates a channel fault.
steps: Play a mono 1 kHz tone through channel 1, all EQ centre.
Record main output and compare L and R.

tests.title: Channel crosstalk through mixer
tests.why: Poor L/R separation or inter-channel bleed.
steps: Feed L-only signal; measure R at main out; repeat.

tests.title: Hum with phono connected
tests.why: Ground-loop hum when turntables connect to the phono input.
steps: Connect turntable and its ground wire to the mixer ground terminal.
Fader up, platter running, stylus lifted; run the test.
Test with the ground wire disconnected for comparison.

tests.title: VCF filter (high-pass/low-pass) sweep
tests.why: The Xone filter is voltage controlled with frequency and resonance; faulty pots cause jumps.
steps: Engage the filter on a channel / master as available.
Sweep frequency knob end to end: smooth sweep, nominal 20 Hz to 20 kHz range.
Increase resonance: self-oscillation at max is normal on Xone filters; no crackle.

tests.title: Crossfader: travel and curve switch
tests.why: Crossfader wear causes channel dropout, hence scratching noise.
steps: Play different sources on channels 1 and 2 with assign switches set to crossfader.
Move the crossfader end to end slowly: no crackle or dropouts, both ends silent.
Flip the curve switch (gradual / sharp): cut-in point should move towards the edge.
Test with fader reverse switch if present.

tests.title: Headphone cue and split
tests.why: Cue routing faults are hard to see on the main output.
steps: Press CUE on channel 1 and then 2: only that channel is in the headphones.
Turn the cue mix / master knob: blends cue and master.
Check cue volume: no hiss at low levels, no crackle when rotating.

tests.title: Outputs: XLR main, booth, record
tests.why: Each output is a separate stage.
steps: Record each output in turn with the same source; compare levels and noise.

tests.title: Mic input and talkover
tests.why: Optional but included in channel features.
steps: Connect a dynamic mic; speak; confirm level, EQ and no hum.

tests.title: Switches, jacks and pots
tests.why: Dust and wear are the typical faults in mixers.
steps: Wiggle each RCA/XLR/jack under signal: no crackle.
Toggle every input and assign switch; confirm the LED/function.
Rotate every pot through its range with music playing.

tests.title: USB driver installed and healthy
tests.why: Without the A&H driver the soundcard channels are not available to Traktor.
steps: Connect the 23C directly to a USB port on the PC (no hub) and switch it on.
Run the driver check.
If missing, install the XONE:23C USB ASIO driver from Allen & Heath and reboot.

pass.source: DeckChek logical presence check (not a published spec)

tests.title: Driver signature
tests.why: An unsigned or legacy driver may be blocked by Windows 10/11.
steps: Run the driver check and read the signature result.

tests.title: Device status OK (no Code 10/43)
tests.why: Catches failed enumeration, power or cable faults.
steps: Run the driver check; open Device Manager if status is not OK.

tests.title: ASIO driver registered
tests.why: Traktor needs the ASIO driver to list the 23C in Preferences > Audio Setup.
steps: Run the driver check.
In Traktor Preferences > Audio Setup the Audio Device list should show the XONE:23C USB ASIO entry.

tests.title: USB port, cable and bus
tests.why: Hubs, long cables or a shared USB controller cause dropouts and clicks on the USB soundcard.
steps: Use a short USB cable straight into the PC, not a hub.
Prefer a port on a different controller from storage devices.
Flex the cable at both connectors while audio plays: no dropouts.

tests.title: USB soundcard signal health: PC to mixer (send 1+2, 3+4)
tests.why: Checks that the PC audio reaches the mixer USB channels, in the playback direction.
steps: Select the 23C ASIO device in the app and route a test signal to USB send 1+2, then 3+4.
Set the channel input switch to USB and record the mixer main/record output into the PC with another interface, or use the 23C return path.
Both channels must show signal at similar level, no clipping or dropouts.

tests.title: USB soundcard signal health: mixer to PC (returns)
tests.why: Checks the record/return direction: audio the mixer sends back over USB.
steps: Feed a line or phono source into a mixer channel and set that channel/return source to USB.
Record the 23C as the input device; run signal health on each USB input pair.
Both channels must show signal at similar level, no clipping or dropouts.

tests.title: USB soundcard noise floor
tests.why: Idle noise or interference from the USB bus on the return channels.
steps: Select the 23C as input, no source playing, channel gains at normal.
Run signal health and read the noise floor.

tests.title: Round-trip latency at the working buffer size
tests.why: DVS needs low latency for tight scratching; the A&H driver trades latency against clock jitter (Bit accurate vs Core Audio modes).
steps: Route a USB send back to a USB return through the mixer (or use a loopback via the analog outputs and another input).
Set the driver/ASIO buffer to the working setting and, in the driver panel, try Bit accurate mode for lowest latency.
In Traktor Audio Setup read the reported latency (ms); record it and any dropouts at that buffer.

tests.title: Traktor Pro install and crash/log scan
tests.why: Traktor crash logs often name the audio driver.
steps: Run the software check after a play session.
Open Documents\Native Instruments\Traktor <ver>\Logs for details.

tests.title: Traktor MK2 vinyl timecode on USB inputs: Deck A (33 1/3)
tests.why: Confirms the 23C soundcard returns a decodable quadrature timecode signal from MK2 control vinyl on this USB input pair.
steps: Connect the turntable phono output to the mixer channel PHONO input (ground wire attached) and set the channel source so the signal is returned over USB (DVS/Traktor routing).
In the app select the 23C USB input pair 1/2 and play the MK2 timecode side at 33 1/3 rpm, pitch 0.
Run the check for at least 20 s.

tests.title: Traktor MK2 vinyl timecode on USB inputs: Deck B (33 1/3)
tests.why: Confirms the 23C soundcard returns a decodable quadrature timecode signal from MK2 control vinyl on this USB input pair.
steps: Connect the turntable phono output to the mixer channel PHONO input (ground wire attached) and set the channel source so the signal is returned over USB (DVS/Traktor routing).
In the app select the 23C USB input pair 3/4 and play the MK2 timecode side at 33 1/3 rpm, pitch 0.
Run the check for at least 20 s.

tests.title: Traktor MK2 vinyl timecode on USB inputs at 45 rpm
tests.why: Speed tracking at 45 rpm through the 23C soundcard.
steps: Set the deck to 45 rpm and repeat the check on Deck A.

tests.title: Timecode calibration in Traktor using the 23C
tests.why: The Traktor Timecode Setup scopes show whether level and phono/line gain through the mixer are right for the MK2 vinyl.
steps: In Traktor Preferences > Audio Setup choose the XONE:23C ASIO device; in Timecode Setup choose MK2 for each deck and assign the USB input pairs.
Play the timecode and press Calibrate; both scopes should be clean circles.
Check Absolute, Relative and Internal modes by loading a track.

tests.title: DVS through the mixer line inputs (external interface)
tests.why: Alternative path: when an external interface (e.g. Audio 8 DJ) is used instead of the 23C soundcard, timecode passes through the LINE inputs.
steps: Connect the Traktor interface outputs to mixer channel LINE inputs and play a deck.
Play control vinyl on a turntable into the interface and confirm the returned deck audio is clean on the mixer channel.
